summary: As of 2026-11-25, Docker Desktop 4.100.1 (2026-11-23) is the newest GA and is newer than pin 4.86.0. 4.100.1 is rebranding-only (no Security/Updates/Windows/WSL notes). Windows always-on stack should review before any upgrade: remaining 4.100.0 still ships Compose v5.7.1, migrates the WSL2 engine to single-distro (monodistro) on next start, and fixes bind-mount file locks/ownership/notifications. No Security heading on 4.100.1 or 4.100.0. Remaining in-delta: 4.99.0 Engine v29.9.3 / proxy socket leak / ungraceful shutdown / Windows Update engine-DB corruption / WSL start/DNS, 4.98.0 CVE-2026-98432 / CVE-2026-112917 (WSL 3.0.3+), 4.97.0 CVE-2026-114409 / CVE-2026-99999, and 4.96.3 eMudhra CLI/daemon CA distrust.
relevant_notes: 4.100.1 (2026-11-23) is the newest GA as of this 2026-11-25 watch. Official docs HTML and docker/docs main (build_path /247138/) both lead with 4.100.1. No 4.100.2. Newer than pin 4.86.0. First seen as newest GA on the 2026-11-24 watch; the 2026-11-20 through 2026-11-23 watches led with 4.100.0 (build_path /246961/). The 2026-11-10 through 2026-11-19 watches led with 4.99.0 (build_path /245822/). 4.100.1 has no Updates section (Compose stays v5.7.1 from 4.100.0; Engine stays v29.9.3 / containerd v2.4.2 / Buildx v0.38.1). No Security heading. No Known issues section. No Windows-specific notes. Docker security-announcements still leads with 4.97.0 CVE-2026-114409 / CVE-2026-99999 and the Sandboxes eMudhra refresh — as of 2026-11-25 it still does not list the 4.98.0 CVEs or anything for 4.99.0, 4.100.0, or 4.100.1. Official Desktop notes remain the source of truth.

4.100.1 Bug fixes and enhancements (all platforms): Additional rebranding updates. Unused / skip for this Windows always-on stack — same class as the 4.100.0 new Moby look. No Engine, Compose, WSL, networking, proxy, VirtioFS, restart/unless-stopped, or CVE content in 4.100.1.

4.100.1 has no Security section. Do not invent a 4.100.1 CVE from that silence, and do not invent a completion claim for 4.98.0 CVE-2026-98432 / CVE-2026-112917, 4.97.0 CVE-2026-114409 / CVE-2026-99999, or the 4.96.x eMudhra intermediate-CA distrust. Those remain in-delta from pin 4.86.0. Docker's security-announcements Sandboxes CA refresh is still not a Desktop CVE and does not apply to this host's postgres/api/mcp or *arr containers (no sbx / sandbox recreate action).

Remaining 4.100.0 (2026-11-19): still in-delta under 4.100.1 and still newer than pin 4.86.0. Official docs HTML and docker/docs main (build_path /246961/). Updates section ships Compose v5.7.1 (from 4.99.0's v5.7.0). No Engine, containerd, or Buildx bump named (still Engine v29.9.3 / containerd v2.4.2 / Buildx v0.38.1 from 4.99.0 / 4.96.x; 4.100.1 did not bump them either). No Security heading. No Known issues section. Docker security-announcements still does not list anything for 4.100.0 or 4.100.1.

Remaining 4.100.0 has no Security section. Do not invent a 4.100.0 CVE from that silence, and do not invent a completion claim for 4.98.0 CVE-2026-98432 / CVE-2026-112917, 4.97.0 CVE-2026-114409 / CVE-2026-99999, or the 4.96.x eMudhra intermediate-CA distrust. Those remain in-delta from pin 4.86.0. Docker's security-announcements Sandboxes CA refresh is still not a Desktop CVE and does not apply to this host's postgres/api/mcp or *arr containers (no sbx / sandbox recreate action).

Remaining 4.100.0 Updates: Docker Compose v5.7.1. Directly relevant to endurance-coach docker-compose.yml (postgres/api/mcp, restart: unless-stopped) and media/*arr Compose workloads. This is the first Compose bump since 4.99.0's v5.7.0. Desktop notes do not list Compose bug-fix details.

Remaining 4.100.0 unused / skip Updates: Docker Offload v0.7.47, Docker Hardened Images (dhictl) v0.0.12, Docker Agent v1.156.2. Offload/dhictl/Agent are unused here. No Docker Scout CLI or Docker MCP CLI bump in 4.100.0 (those last moved in 4.99.0 to Scout CLI v1.28.0 / Docker MCP CLI v0.44.3 — Docker MCP CLI is still not the endurance-coach mcp container).

Remaining 4.100.0 all platforms: file locks, ownership changes and file-change notifications were ignored on the descriptor that created a file in a bind mount (desktop-feedback#765). Directly relevant to this Windows always-on stack — media/*arr host bind mounts (library watchers, downloads, music ingest) and endurance-coach ~/.garminconnect plus ~/.endurance-coach mounts. A writer that creates a file then locks, chowns, or expects inotify/fsevents on that same descriptor can miss events or see stale ownership until this fix.

Remaining 4.100.0 Windows: the WSL2 engine now uses single-distro (monodistro) mode by default, automatically migrating legacy dual-distro setups on next start for improved performance. High impact for this always-on WSL host (restart_docker_desktop.ps1 does wsl --shutdown, post_virt_recovery.ps1 talks to wsl -d docker-desktop, configure_docker_wsl_limits.ps1 writes .wslconfig). A dual-distro docker-desktop + docker-desktop-data layout will migrate on the first Desktop start after upgrade — plan a window, snapshot/inspect the WSL data disk first, and expect engine-disk / distro-name changes during that start, not a silent in-place bump.

Remaining 4.100.0 Windows: updating a Hyper-V installation enabled the WSL feature. Relevant if this host is on the Hyper-V backend rather than WSL2 — an upgrade could flip WSL on unexpectedly. This host's usual pin path is WSL2; do not treat that as a reason to switch engines.

Remaining 4.100.0 unused / skip: new Moby-branded look; ECI/kind Kubernetes state loss after Desktop restart; already-downloaded update fetched again after a restart; hang/memory growth when publishing host port 65535 (desktop-feedback#164); allowedOrgs analytics after restart; MCP Toolkit Profiles tab stdout maxBuffer (desktop-feedback#681) — Docker's MCP toolkit, not endurance-coach mcp; docker build API chunked keep-alive hang (desktop-feedback#805); Docker VMM stuck in the stopping state when the VMM process did not exit after the VM powered off; sparse raw disk format (DockerDesktop.raw) for new Docker VMM installs replacing VHDX to prevent meta.db corruption (existing installs unaffected); Restart option on the WSL not installed error; desktop-feedback#820 (Docker VMM engine hang / virtio-console RCU stall — reporter was on Docker VMM, not WSL2); Mac-only privileged-port forwarding with Apple Virtualization; Linux .deb AppArmor LSM. This host runs Linux containers on WSL2, not Docker VMM, kind/ECI, or Windows containers.

Remaining 4.99.0 (2026-11-09): still in-delta under 4.100.1 and still newer than pin 4.86.0. Official docs HTML and docker/docs main (build_path /245822/). Updates section shipped Compose v5.7.0 (now superseded by 4.100.0's v5.7.1) and Engine v29.9.3 (still current — 4.100.0 and 4.100.1 did not bump Engine). No containerd or Buildx bump named (still containerd v2.4.2 / Buildx v0.38.1). No Security heading. No Known issues section. Docker security-announcements still does not list anything for 4.99.0.

Remaining 4.99.0 has no Security section. Do not invent a 4.99.0 CVE from that silence. 4.98.0 CVE-2026-98432 / CVE-2026-112917, 4.97.0 CVE-2026-114409 / CVE-2026-99999, and the 4.96.x eMudhra intermediate-CA distrust remain in-delta from pin 4.86.0.
Remaining 4.99.0 Updates: Docker Compose v5.7.0, now superseded for the review target by 4.100.0's Compose v5.7.1. Desktop notes did not list Compose bug-fix details for either bump.

Remaining 4.99.0 Updates: Docker Engine v29.9.3. First Engine bump since 4.96.1's 29.9.2, and still the Engine version in 4.100.1. Directly relevant to this always-on Windows stack (container runtime for postgres/api/mcp and *arr). Desktop notes do not list Engine CVE/bug-fix details beyond the version bump.

Remaining 4.99.0 unused / skip Updates: Docker Offload v0.7.36, Docker Hardened Images (dhictl) v0.0.10, Docker Agent v1.153.0, Docker Scout CLI v1.28.0, Docker MCP CLI v0.44.3. Offload/dhictl/Agent/Scout are unused here. Docker MCP CLI is Docker's MCP toolkit, not the endurance-coach mcp container — do not treat v0.44.3 as a coach-mcp change.

Remaining 4.99.0 all platforms: socket leak in the system proxy where plain HTTP requests from containers routed through an upstream proxy left one socket open per request until restart. Directly relevant to this ExpressVPN / proxy-adjacent always-on host — *arr indexers, image pulls, and coach outbound HTTP through Desktop's system proxy can leak sockets until Docker Desktop is restarted.

Remaining 4.99.0 all platforms: Docker Desktop could shut down ungracefully, causing resource leaks or a corrupted state by not allowing cleanup handlers to run. Directly relevant to restart / unless-stopped / heal_full_stack.ps1 / restart_docker_desktop.ps1 / Windows Update / power-loss on this always-on host (configure_power_outage_hardening.ps1, post_boot_stack_recovery.ps1).

Remaining 4.99.0 Windows: Windows updates stopping Docker Desktop abruptly, which could corrupt the engine databases. High impact for this always-on Windows stack — a host Windows Update can kill Desktop mid-run and corrupt engine DBs that recover *arr Compose and endurance-coach postgres/api/mcp. Related to remaining 4.91.0 abrupt-shutdown network-DB recovery.

Remaining 4.99.0 Windows: WSL 2 engine start failing on slow machines when the data disk took more than a fraction of a second to appear. Directly relevant to this WSL host after reboot / wsl --shutdown / restart_docker_desktop.ps1 / heal_full_stack.ps1 — a slow data-disk attach could leave postgres/api/mcp and *arr down even though WSL was coming up. 4.100.0's monodistro migration on next start makes a healthy first post-upgrade engine start more important, not less.

Remaining 4.99.0 Windows: WSL 2 distributions flushed their systemd-resolved DNS cache every 30 seconds while Docker Desktop was running (desktop-feedback#761). Networking-relevant on this WSL2 always-on host — periodic DNS cache flushes can stall *arr indexer/download traffic, image pulls, and endurance-coach outbound calls.

Remaining 4.99.0 Windows: per-user installs and updates failed with a Virtual Machine Platform error on machines where WSL 2 already works. Relevant to scripts/update_docker_desktop.ps1 if this host's install is per-user; a false VMP error can block a planned upgrade even though WSL 2 is already healthy (post_virt_recovery.ps1 checks VMP + WSL features).

Remaining 4.99.0 Windows: Docker Desktop hung after closing an error dialog with its Close button. Closing an error dialog that offers Continue now continues instead of quitting Docker Desktop. Recovery-adjacent for heal_full_stack.ps1 / restart_docker_desktop.ps1 when an error dialog is on screen.

Remaining 4.99.0 Windows: installer launcher now reports descriptive error reasons (for example Disk full) on update failure instead of a bare exit code. Helps diagnose winget upgrade --id Docker.DockerDesktop in update_docker_desktop.ps1.

Remaining 4.99.0 all platforms: constant network traffic and CPU usage from Docker Desktop computing the size of NFS- or SMB-backed volumes (desktop-feedback#800). Only relevant if this host uses NFS/SMB-backed Docker volumes for media/*arr or coach data; skip if volumes are local WSL/ext4 or bind mounts.

Remaining 4.99.0 unused / skip: Containers list cutting off ports on Show all ports (desktop-feedback#794); connection resets on published ports under bursts of new connections with Docker VMM; Mac-only installer killed while quitting; BuildKit for Windows containers with the containerd image store; docker desktop commands from inside a WSL distro; Windows containers failing to start at login when a container took longer than 30 seconds to stop. This host runs Linux containers (endurance-coach postgres/api/mcp + media/*arr) on WSL2, not Windows containers or Docker VMM.

Remaining 4.98.0 (2026-11-03): still in-delta under 4.100.1 and still newer than pin 4.86.0. Official notes include a Security section naming CVE-2026-98432 and CVE-2026-112917. Updates section was Offload v0.7.35 plus Kubernetes image tags only — no Engine, containerd, Compose, or Buildx bump in 4.98.0 itself (Engine 29.9.2 / containerd v2.4.2 / Compose v5.6.1 until 4.99.0). No Known issues section. Docker security-announcements still does not list the 4.98.0 CVEs.

Remaining 4.98.0 security: fixed CVE-2026-98432, a use-after-free in the Linux kernel's IPv4 TCP handling. Official Desktop notes name this CVE; it is not a third-party attribution. Directly relevant to this always-on Windows stack: media/*arr Compose, endurance-coach postgres/api/mcp, ExpressVPN/LAN next to those containers, and published ports 5432/8000/8080 plus media ports. A kernel TCP use-after-free can take down Docker/WSL networking rather than only one container.

Remaining 4.98.0 security: fixed CVE-2026-112917 where a container on the WSL 2 backend could bypass the AF_VSOCK restriction. Official Desktop notes say this requires WSL 3.0.3 or later. Directly relevant to this WSL2 always-on host — an *arr or coach container that can reach AF_VSOCK can talk past Desktop isolation to host-facing services. A Desktop-only upgrade without WSL 3.0.3 is not the full official fix. Do not add third-party CVSS or socketcall write-ups; stick to the official Desktop sentence.

Remaining 4.98.0 Security section names CVE-2026-98432 and CVE-2026-112917 only. It does not mention CVE-2026-114409, CVE-2026-99999, or the eMudhra intermediate-CA distrust. Do not invent a completion claim from that silence. Those 4.97.0 / 4.96.x items remain in-delta from pin 4.86.0.

Remaining 4.98.0 all platforms: Docker Desktop stayed on the Starting page after Docker Engine had already started (desktop-feedback#685). Directly relevant to this always-on media + coach host — post_boot_stack_recovery.ps1 / heal_full_stack.ps1 / unless-stopped recovery can look hung even when the engine is up.

Remaining 4.98.0 all platforms: uncaught Request aborted errors each time the engine stopped. Restart / unless-stopped / heal_full_stack.ps1 / restart_docker_desktop.ps1 stop-start cycles on this host fire that path.

Remaining 4.98.0 all platforms: diagnose gather on slow or stopped VMs now caps the VM start wait at 120 seconds. Helps heal_full_stack.ps1 / restart_docker_desktop.ps1 diagnosis when the engine is hung (related to the remaining 4.97.0 diagnostics-when-unresponsive speedup).

Remaining 4.98.0 all platforms: moving the disk image to another volume failed when the copy took more than 5 minutes. Relevant if this host relocates the WSL/engine disk (also still in-delta: 4.97.0 move-back #565, 4.92.0 move-to-other-drive #548/#550). Snapshot that disk before the 4.100.0 monodistro migration as well.

Remaining 4.98.0 all platforms: Docker Hub model pulls failed on proxy-only networks where local DNS could not resolve the authentication endpoint. Proxy-adjacent on this ExpressVPN host, but it is model-pull auth DNS, not general image pulls for postgres/api/mcp or *arr. Low stack impact.

Remaining 4.98.0 Windows: WSL error code parsing now gives accurate recovery instructions on newer WSL 3.0.x instead of a generic error. Relevant to this WSL host, configure_docker_wsl_limits.ps1, and the remaining 4.96.0 'bad magic string' / 4.97.0 Wsl/CallMsi/ misread notes. Also the official CVE-2026-112917 fix requires WSL 3.0.3 or later, so this host may be on or moving to 3.0.x.

Remaining 4.98.0 Windows: intermittent Being used by another process error on the desktop-linux Docker context file when the engine started. Can stall engine start / unless-stopped recovery after reboot or heal_full_stack.ps1.

Remaining 4.98.0 Windows: file sharing treated a directory as shared, or as allowed by Settings Management, when its name only started with that of a shared or allowed directory (for example C:\foobar for C:\foo). Whole directory names only now. VirtioFS / file-sharing / bind-mount adjacent for media/*arr host paths and endurance-coach ~/.garminconnect plus ~/.endurance-coach. Confirm share prefixes are not accidentally covering a sibling directory, and that the intended share still matches after the exact-name change. Related to the new 4.100.0 bind-mount lock/ownership/notification fix (#765).

Remaining 4.98.0 Windows unused / skip: Docker VMM added to the Clean up data dialog; Docker VMM backend option on Windows ARM64 now disabled with an explanation and falls back to WSL 2; docker and docker compose from WSL 2 distros when Docker VMM is the engine (including /mnt/c bind mounts); Docker VMM re-enabling the WSL feature on update and showing Press any key to install WSL when WSL is uninstalled (desktop-feedback#775). This host's pin path is WSL2 + winget, not Docker VMM or ARM64. Do not switch this always-on WSL stack to Docker VMM from this alert. 4.100.0's Hyper-V-update-enabled-WSL fix is a related Hyper-V-install note, not a reason to change engines.

Remaining 4.98.0 unused / skip: Docker Offload v0.7.35; Kubernetes image tag bumps (desktop-storage-provisioner v5.0, desktop-vpnkit-controller v5.0, desktop-containerd-registry-mirror v0.0.5, desktop-cloud-provider-kind v0.8.0); error-dialog responsiveness; processes left running after closing the Docker Desktop terminal; Mac-only removal of com.docker.vmnetd. Not this Windows always-on media/*arr + endurance-coach stack.

Remaining 4.97.0 (2026-10-26): bug-fix / enhancement release with no Updates section (no Engine, containerd, Compose, or Buildx bump). Official notes include a Security section naming CVE-2026-114409 and CVE-2026-99999. No Known issues section. Still newer than pin 4.86.0 and still in-delta under 4.100.1.

Remaining 4.97.0 Windows: Docker Desktop became unresponsive, with docker commands hanging and Quit not working, after the disk filled up or, on Windows, after the backend's console host process exited (desktop-feedback#429 and #699). Directly relevant to this always-on media + coach host — a full WSL/engine disk or a crashed console host could leave postgres/api/mcp and *arr unreachable with no working Quit / heal path.

Remaining 4.97.0 Windows: a slow WSL version check asked to update WSL. Relevant to this WSL host and configure_docker_wsl_limits.ps1 (which also runs wsl --update). A false or premature update prompt can stall engine start / unless-stopped recovery. 4.98.0's WSL 3.0.x error-code parsing and the CVE-2026-112917 WSL 3.0.3 requirement make an accurate WSL version check more important, not less.

Remaining 4.97.0 Windows: WSL installer errors (for example Wsl/CallMsi/) were misidentified as disk-related failures, producing a misleading 'disk file has been deleted' recovery message. Related to the remaining 4.92.0 misleading WSL disk-image-deleted error. Do not treat that dialog as proof the engine disk (media/*arr volumes + endurance-coach postgres_data) is gone.

Remaining 4.97.0 Windows: Docker VMM required a Docker Desktop restart to share a new bind-mount directory from the host. Bind-mount / VirtioFS-adjacent. Relevant if this host uses Docker VMM rather than WSL2; endurance-coach host mounts (~/.garminconnect, ~/.endurance-coach) and media/*arr bind mounts would not appear until a Desktop restart.

Remaining 4.97.0 Windows: the installer now offers a Docker VMM (Beta) backend option, and --user mode is now the default for new Docker Desktop .EXE installations. This host's pin path is winget upgrade --id Docker.DockerDesktop, not a fresh .EXE. Do not switch this always-on WSL stack to Docker VMM from this alert; leave that for a human. Installer also rejected --backend=docker-vmm when combined with --user or Microsoft Store installs (fixed in 4.97.0).

Remaining 4.97.0 Windows: factory reset now stops Docker engines before deleting data, surfaces cleanup failures as an error dialog, and cleans custom data-root directories. Recovery-relevant if a human later factory-resets after a bad upgrade (media/*arr volumes + postgres_data).

Remaining 4.97.0 Windows: the installer could leave a file under C:\ProgramData\DockerDesktop with no permissions, making it unreadable to diagnostics and later installs. Relevant to scripts/update_docker_desktop.ps1 and diagnostics after a failed or partial upgrade.

Remaining 4.97.0 Windows: the disk image location could not be moved back to a folder it had previously been moved out of (desktop-feedback#565). Relevant if this host relocates the WSL/engine disk. Also a failed update could restore Start Menu and desktop shortcuts that had been deleted on purpose (low stack impact).

Remaining 4.97.0 Windows (not this stack): Windows containers failed to start with a "Path contains symlink" error on callback.sock. This host runs Linux containers (endurance-coach postgres/api/mcp + media/*arr), not Windows containers.

Remaining 4.97.0 all platforms: diagnostics collection when the backend was unresponsive dropped from several minutes to about 3 seconds. Helps heal_full_stack.ps1 / restart_docker_desktop.ps1 diagnosis when the engine is hung.

Remaining 4.97.0 all platforms: Date header in Docker API responses was incorrect after Resource Saver mode. Mildly relevant if this host uses Resource Saver (also still in-delta: 4.94.0 Resource Saver pause-before-API-ready, 4.91.0 Compose rebuild on wake).

Remaining 4.97.0 all platforms: unhandled error when viewing files of a Compose project whose config file no longer exists. Dashboard/Compose-adjacent; not a compose runtime change for endurance-coach docker-compose.yml or media/*arr.

Remaining 4.97.0 unused / skip: docker pass run -e/--env and docker pass set Ctrl-C; Images/Containers/Volumes search responsiveness; container exec terminal reliability; Resource Saver error when signing out with sign-in enforcement. Mac-only: fish PATH, privileged ports 1–1024 on LAN. Not this Windows always-on stack.

Remaining 4.97.0 security: addressed CVE-2026-114409, where Docker Desktop could write third-party API keys and OAuth access tokens in cleartext to local application logs and diagnostics bundles (insufficient IPC payload redaction). These OAuth tokens are not Docker account tokens. Official security-announcements say 4.94.0 and 4.95.0 addressed the known logging paths, but leftover logs and crash dumps can remain after upgrading; 4.97.0 also cleans existing host logs and crash dumps. If this host generated or shared diagnostics bundles with Docker Desktop 4.96.x or earlier, or kept copies of Docker Desktop logs elsewhere, delete or sanitize them. Relevant to this always-on host's Desktop logs/IPC; Garmin/Strava/Whoop tokens live in host-mounted ~/.garminconnect and ~/.endurance-coach and are not typically Desktop IPC, but leftover Desktop logs/bundles should still be reviewed.

Remaining 4.97.0 security: addressed CVE-2026-99999, a kernel vulnerability where a container could exploit bad IPv4 checksum metadata via TUN or AF_PACKET to corrupt the VM's network stack. Directly relevant to this always-on Windows stack: media/*arr Compose, endurance-coach postgres/api/mcp, ExpressVPN/LAN next to those containers, and published ports 5432/8000/8080 plus media ports. A successful exploit would take down Docker networking rather than only one container. Official Desktop notes and security-announcements both name this CVE; it is not a third-party attribution.

Remaining 4.96.3 (2026-10-22): same-day patch after 4.96.2. Ships Docker Init v1.4.1, Docker Offload v0.7.19, Docker Model Runner v1.2.9, Docker Debug v0.49.0, Docker MCP v0.44.2, and kubectl v1.36.1. Init/Offload/Model Runner/Debug/kubectl are unused by this media/*arr + endurance-coach stack. Docker MCP here is Docker's MCP toolkit, not the endurance-coach mcp container — do not treat the v0.44.2 bump as a coach-mcp change. No Engine, containerd, Compose, or Buildx bump in 4.96.3 itself (those landed in 4.96.2 / 4.96.1 / 4.96.0). 4.97.0 and 4.98.0 also had no Engine/containerd/Compose/Buildx bump; 4.99.0 bumped Engine 29.9.3 / Compose v5.7.0; 4.100.0 bumps Compose again to v5.7.1 and still does not bump Engine/containerd/Buildx; 4.100.1 has no Updates section and does not bump them either. No Known issues section. No named CVE id in the 4.96.3 notes.

Remaining 4.96.3 / 4.96.2 / 4.96.1 security: removed trust for certificates issued by the compromised eMudhra intermediate CA. An attacker with network access could intercept TLS connections made by non-browser clients such as the Docker CLI and daemon. Directly relevant to this always-on Windows stack (image pulls, Compose, registry/auth, ExpressVPN/LAN next to media/*arr and endurance-coach). Official Desktop notes do not assign a CVE id. Do not add third-party CVE numbers. Docker's security-announcements page also covers a Sandboxes-only CA refresh — this host's postgres/api/mcp and *arr containers are not Docker Sandboxes; do not treat sandbox recreate / sbx --pull always as a stack action.

Remaining 4.96.1 / 4.96.2 IMPORTANT: the eMudhra CA distrust is rolling out in batches as individual Docker Desktop components are updated. Upcoming patch releases will cover remaining components; Docker recommends taking each patch as it becomes available. 4.96.3 is the next same-day batch (Init / Offload / Model Runner / Debug / MCP / kubectl) and repeats the CA security paragraph, but it does not repeat the 'upcoming patches' IMPORTANT callout. 4.97.0 names CVE-2026-114409 and CVE-2026-99999, 4.98.0 names CVE-2026-98432 and CVE-2026-112917, and 4.99.0 / 4.100.0 / 4.100.1 have no Security heading — none of those mention eMudhra or remaining batches. Do not invent a completion claim from that silence. Leave the pin at 4.86.0; a human should decide whether to take 4.100.1 now.

Remaining 4.96.2 (2026-10-22): Compose v5.6.1 (from 4.95.0's v5.6.0), superseded for the review target by 4.100.0's Compose v5.7.1. Also Docker Offload v0.7.6, Docker Agent v1.152.0, Docker Hardened Images CLI (dhictl) v0.0.9, Docker Desktop Build v0.39.1, and Docker Scout CLI v1.27.0 — Offload/Agent/dhictl/Build/Scout are not used by this media/*arr + endurance-coach stack. Same eMudhra CA security note as 4.96.3 (with the batched IMPORTANT callout that 4.96.3 omits). No Known issues section. No named CVE id.

Remaining 4.96.1 (2026-10-21): Engine 29.9.2 (from 4.96.0's v29.9.1), superseded for the review target by 4.99.0's Engine v29.9.3 (still current in 4.100.0). Also Buildx v0.38.1 (from v0.38.0), Credential helpers v0.9.12 (from 4.96.0's v0.9.10), Docker Offload v0.7.16. Same eMudhra CA security note as 4.96.2 (first batch of the CA distrust). No Known issues section. No named CVE id. Credential-helper bump matters if this host uses docker login / registry auth for image pulls.

Remaining 4.96.0 (2026-10-19): Engine v29.9.1 (from 4.94.0's v29.8.2), containerd v2.4.2 (from 4.94.0's v2.3.6), Buildx v0.38.0 (from 4.94.0's v0.37.2), and Credential helpers v0.9.10 (superseded by 4.96.1's v0.9.12). Compose was still v5.6.0 until 4.96.2. No Known issues section on 4.96.0. No named CVE id in the 4.96.0 notes.

Remaining 4.96.0 all platforms: Docker Desktop's internal DHCP replies were sent onto the host's physical network. Networking-relevant on this always-on Windows host (ExpressVPN media stack + LAN access in configure_expressvpn_media_stack.ps1); leaked DHCP can confuse LAN/VPN routing next to media/*arr and endurance-coach published ports.

Remaining 4.96.0 all platforms: Docker Desktop got stuck on 'Starting the Docker Engine...' when a Docker network took addresses inside Docker Desktop's internal network (192.168.65.0/24 by default). Overlapping networks are now rejected, and an existing one can be removed from the error dialog (desktop-feedback#659). endurance-coach compose has no custom subnet; check media/*arr Compose networks for 192.168.65.0/24 overlap before upgrade, or engine start / unless-stopped recovery can hang. Related to the remaining 4.98.0 Starting-page-after-engine-up fix (#685).

Remaining 4.96.0 Windows: an unusable WSL data disk (for example already in use) repeatedly triggered failed mkfs format attempts instead of a clear error. Directly relevant to this always-on WSL host — a busy or locked engine disk could have been re-formatted (media/*arr volumes + endurance-coach postgres_data). Snapshot that disk before the 4.100.0 monodistro migration.

Remaining 4.96.0 Windows: WSL distro startup failures showed a confusing 'bad magic string' error instead of the actual reason reported by wsl.exe. Improves WSL diagnosis for configure_docker_wsl_limits.ps1 / restart_docker_desktop.ps1 / heal_full_stack.ps1. 4.98.0 further improves WSL 3.0.x error-code parsing.

Remaining 4.96.0 Windows: full-disk errors during startup now show the disk-full recovery dialog instead of a generic failure. Useful on this media + coach host if the WSL/engine disk or host volume fills.
Remaining 4.96.0 Windows: clearer error when Docker VMM cannot use the Windows hypervisor (for example some VMs where WSL 2 works). Relevant only if this host uses Docker VMM rather than WSL2.

Remaining 4.96.0 all platforms: the error dialog could close unexpectedly on systems under memory pressure. Affects restart / recovery visibility on this always-on media + coach host after a RAM-tight reboot.

Remaining 4.96.0 Mac-only: file ownership and transient 0:0 reporting on Apple Virtualization Framework + VirtioFS bind mounts (desktop-feedback#628/#649). Not a Windows VirtioFS fix; the Windows 4.90.0 bind-mount 0:0 note remains in-delta for ~/.garminconnect, ~/.endurance-coach, and media/*arr mounts. Related to the new 4.100.0 bind-mount lock/ownership/notification fix (#765), which is not Mac-only.

Remaining 4.96.0 all platforms: improved buffered filesystem performance and a FUSE fix that could expose stale bytes when extending files. Filesystem-adjacent; do not treat as a Windows VirtioFS claim.

Remaining 4.96.0 all platforms: backend crashed and the engine became unreachable when a container's --volumes-from referred back to itself (desktop-feedback#286). endurance-coach and typical *arr Compose do not use that rename/volumes-from pattern.
Remaining 4.95.0 (2026-10-12): Compose v5.6.0 (from 4.91.0's v5.5.1). No Engine / containerd / Buildx bump in the 4.95.0 notes themselves. No Known issues section. No named CVE id.

Remaining 4.95.0 Windows: the installer deleted the WSL data disk during an update when the data root was inside the Docker Desktop installation directory (desktop-feedback#667). Directly relevant to this always-on WSL host and scripts/update_docker_desktop.ps1 — a bad disk-image path can wipe the engine disk (media/*arr volumes + endurance-coach postgres_data) on upgrade.

Remaining 4.95.0 all platforms: Settings accepted a disk image location inside the Docker Desktop installation directory, which the installer replaces on every update (same desktop-feedback#667). Confirm the WSL/Hyper-V disk image is not under Program Files\Docker before any upgrade.
Remaining 4.95.0 Windows: updates could fail because app.asar was reported as locked by Docker Desktop. Directly relevant to winget upgrade --id Docker.DockerDesktop in update_docker_desktop.ps1.

Remaining 4.95.0 Windows: Hyper-V VM could fail to start after a restart because its disk was still being compacted. Affects restart / unless-stopped / heal_full_stack.ps1 / restart_docker_desktop.ps1 if this host is on Hyper-V rather than WSL2.

Remaining 4.95.0 Windows: Docker Desktop failed to start with the Hyper-V backend when the Windows hosts file was protected by an antivirus or endpoint security tool. Networking / name-resolution risk on a hardened always-on host.

Remaining 4.95.0 Windows: dedicated error when the Hyper-V VM cannot start because the host does not have enough free memory. Useful on this always-on media + coach host if RAM is tight after a reboot.

Remaining 4.95.0 Windows: WSL 3.0.1 reported docker info as 'Docker Desktop (containerized)' instead of 'Docker Desktop', which broke docker debug when Registry Access Management was enabled. WSL-relevant if this host has moved to WSL 3.0.1; 4.98.0's CVE-2026-112917 fix wants WSL 3.0.3 or later.

Remaining 4.95.0 Windows: WSL/MSYS2 native symlink (LX symlink) handling, sparse stream exports via backup tar, and a named-pipe listener-close race were fixed. Applies to media/*arr and endurance-coach host bind mounts that use symlinks or WSL paths.

Remaining 4.95.0 all platforms: Quit did nothing in the engine-failed error dialog, and that dialog took around 2 minutes to appear when the engine failed while starting. Gathering diagnostics from the same dialog failed repeatedly when Docker Desktop could not start. Affects restart / recovery visibility for post_boot_stack_recovery.ps1 and heal_full_stack.ps1.

Remaining 4.95.0 Windows installer: intermittent MSI 1603 from analytics custom actions racing other installer steps; per-user install silently completed when Virtual Machine Platform was disabled (Desktop then could not start); per-user install from SYSTEM (SCCM/Intune) now fails with an explicit error instead of installing into the SYSTEM profile. This host's pin path is winget, not MSI/SCCM.

Remaining 4.95.0 all platforms: engine restarted right after Docker Desktop started when an admin policy enabled Enhanced Container Isolation. Only relevant if this host is under a Docker org admin policy.

Remaining 4.94.0 Windows: Docker Desktop service lost its automatic start mode after a WinGet or other external-installer update when the service had been installed with --always-run-service. Directly relevant to this always-on host and scripts/update_docker_desktop.ps1 (winget upgrade --id Docker.DockerDesktop).

Remaining 4.94.0 Windows: fixed the 4.92.0 bug where WSL integration failed to start with 'timed out waiting for ... to be automounted' (desktop-feedback#695). This is the explicit fix for the 4.92.0 known issue (wsl.conf [automount] root=/ or a container bind-mounting a non-drive /mnt path such as /mnt/wslg). 4.93.0 already had a related WSL bind-mount proxy fatal-timeout fix; 4.94.0 names the automount-timeout failure directly.

Remaining 4.94.0 all platforms: Resource Saver could pause the VM before the Docker API was ready, causing transient errors during engine startup or restart. Relevant to always-on restart / unless-stopped / heal_full_stack.ps1 / Resource Saver wake (endurance-coach api/mcp use build: .).

Remaining 4.94.0 all platforms: Docker Desktop service was left stopped after an update when it was running but not configured to auto-start. Always-on stacks that expect the engine to come back after an update can stay down until a human starts the service.

Remaining 4.94.0 security: stored API keys were written in clear to Docker Desktop logs and included in diagnostics bundles. Logs also recorded unobfuscated values for IPC payloads that were JSON arrays or plain strings. Official security-announcements now assign CVE-2026-114409: 4.94.0 and 4.95.0 addressed the known logging paths, but leftover logs can remain; 4.97.0 fixes remaining redaction and cleans existing host logs and crash dumps. Review and delete or sanitize any diagnostics bundles generated on 4.96.x or earlier.

Remaining 4.94.0 all platforms: Docker Desktop could write a multi-gigabyte error file and consume excessive memory when the backend failed to start. Always-on host disk/RAM risk after a failed engine start.

Remaining 4.94.0 all platforms: default logging driver for new Linux containers changed to local (automatic log rotation, lower disk use). endurance-coach compose already sets logging.driver: local with max-size 10m / max-file 3; media/*arr Compose that omit a logging driver will pick up the new default only for newly created containers.

Remaining 4.94.0 Windows: WSL startup errors now explain when virtualization is disabled in firmware, nested virtualization is unavailable, or the Windows hypervisor is disabled at startup, with guidance for each condition.
Remaining 4.94.0 all platforms: invalid JSON in a settings file now names the file that needs correcting instead of an unexpected error. Helpful if recovery/hardening scripts rewrite Docker config.

Remaining 4.93.0 all platforms: Docker Desktop failed to start with an unexpected error when the engine needed more than five minutes to recover after an unclean shutdown. Directly relevant to this always-on host (configure_power_outage_hardening.ps1, post_boot_stack_recovery.ps1, restart_docker_desktop.ps1).

Remaining 4.93.0 Windows: WSL integration proxy could fatally timeout at startup when restoring persisted bind mounts, especially with non-default wsl.conf [automount] root. Related to the 4.92.0 known issue that 4.94.0 now explicitly fixes. Review wsl.conf and media/*arr plus endurance-coach host bind mounts before upgrading.

Remaining 4.93.0 Windows: a failed read of a WSL distro's config.json crashed the distro agent, disabled WSL integration, and prevented factory reset from cleaning ~/.docker. Can leave the engine/integration dead after a bad or partial distro config.

Remaining 4.93.0 Windows: spurious 'WSL integration with distro unexpectedly stopped' dialogs fired while the engine was being stopped or restarted. Affects restart / unless-stopped / heal_full_stack.ps1 stop-start cycles.

Remaining 4.93.0 Windows: unhelpful error when WSL timed out registering the Docker Desktop Linux distribution; false 'Virtualization support not detected' when Virtual Machine Platform was enabled but vfpext was absent; WSL2 CLI credential store could reset to default on restart.

Remaining 4.93.0 Windows: startup crash (exit code 151) when settings-store.json or daemon.json was saved with a UTF-8 BOM by an external editor or provisioning tool. enable_docker_autostart.ps1 uses Set-Content -Encoding UTF8 on those settings files (Windows PowerShell 5.x writes a BOM).

Remaining 4.93.0 all platforms: file sharing directories (and other list settings) reverted to defaults after they were cleared and Docker Desktop restarted (desktop-feedback#515). VirtioFS / shared-folder settings for media/*arr bind mounts can silently reset.
Remaining 4.93.0 security: VM-side code could request Unix socket port forwards, which could expose arbitrary host paths to manipulation. Also Engine v29.8.1. No named CVE id in the 4.93.0 notes.

Remaining 4.93.0 Windows upgrade path: MSI installs never added the installing user to docker-users; update failures showed a generic error instead of installer details. This host's pin path is winget (update_docker_desktop.ps1), not MSI.

Remaining 4.92.0 all platforms: published ports stayed unreachable for the life of the container when the host port was momentarily busy. Directly relevant to endurance-coach 5432/8000/8080 and media ports (Jellyfin 8096, Caddy 443, Sonarr 8989, Radarr 7878, Prowlarr 9696, Navidrome 4533, slskd 5030) during heal/restart races.

Remaining 4.92.0 Windows: WSL 2 cross-distro bind-mount proxy could serve stale or incomplete directory contents for host paths on slow-to-mount drives (example: Storage Pool volumes). Applies to media/*arr bind mounts and endurance-coach host mounts (${USERPROFILE}/.garminconnect, ${USERPROFILE}/.endurance-coach).

Remaining 4.92.0 Windows: Docker Desktop retried the WSL engine indefinitely without reporting an error when WSL could not load its own kernel modules; a misleading error claimed the WSL disk image had been deleted when WSL could not open it while registering the distribution.

Remaining 4.92.0 Windows: Windows 10 hosts with inbox wsl.exe saw a raw error instead of the prompt to update WSL. Relevant if this host still uses inbox WSL (configure_docker_wsl_limits.ps1 also runs wsl --update).

Remaining 4.92.0 Windows: single-file bind mounts on Docker VMM were broken; disk image location moves to a different drive always failed (desktop-feedback#548/#550). Relevant only if this host uses Docker VMM or relocates the disk image.
Remaining 4.92.0 all platforms: Send Diagnostics hung or showed an unhelpful error when a proxy blocked the upload. Proxy-related; this host also uses ExpressVPN.

Remaining 4.92.0 security: containerd updated to v2.3.5, addressing CVE-2026-53495. 4.94.0 further updates containerd to v2.3.6 (no additional CVE named). 4.96.0 bumps containerd again to v2.4.2 with no additional named CVE in the Desktop notes. 4.96.1 / 4.96.2 / 4.96.3 / 4.97.0 / 4.98.0 / 4.99.0 / 4.100.0 / 4.100.1 do not bump containerd further.

Remaining 4.91.0 all platforms: a corrupt Docker network database, usually from an abrupt shutdown, prevented Docker Engine from starting and left a factory reset as the only recovery option. Directly relevant to this always-on host. 4.99.0 separately fixes Windows Update killing Desktop and corrupting engine databases.

Remaining 4.91.0 all platforms: Docker Compose rebuilt locally-built images on every Resource Saver wake (docker/desktop-feedback#507). endurance-coach compose uses build: . / image: endurance-coach:latest for api and mcp.

Remaining 4.91.0 all platforms: the VM could shut down unexpectedly when idle timeout was set to 0; Docker Desktop sometimes took five extra minutes to report the engine as stopped when the VM stopped unexpectedly. Affects always-on idle/auto-pause and restart/unless-stopped recovery timing.

Remaining 4.91.0 Windows: Docker Desktop stayed on Starting... indefinitely when WSL could not access the disk image location; it now reports the access failure with guidance instead of a generic WSL error.

Remaining 4.90.0 Windows: startup hang on 'Starting' after a WinGet upgrade when install-settings.json has conflicting engine settings. Directly relevant to scripts/update_docker_desktop.ps1 (winget upgrade --id Docker.DockerDesktop).

Remaining 4.90.0 / 4.89.0 Windows: Docker Desktop could fail to start after an ungraceful shutdown left a stuck socket. Relevant to power-loss recovery. Related to the remaining 4.99.0 ungraceful-shutdown cleanup-handler fix.

Remaining 4.90.0 Windows: a failing third-party WSL plugin (example: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint WSL plugin) was reported as a missing Docker Desktop disk instead of naming the plugin that blocked WSL.

Remaining 4.90.0 all platforms: bind-mount root intermittently reported ownership 0:0 (git 'detected dubious ownership'); repeatedly replacing files on a shared folder leaked VM disk space; VirtioFS renameat2(RENAME_EXCHANGE) overwrote the target; mmap() of a Synchronized File Share file failed. Applies to endurance-coach host mounts and media/*arr bind mounts. Related to the new 4.100.0 bind-mount lock/ownership/notification fix (#765).

Remaining 4.90.0 security: Kind cloud provider image v0.7.0 addresses CVE-2026-46595 and CVE-2026-39834. Low priority unless this host uses Kind / Docker Offload Kubernetes. 4.98.0 later retags desktop-cloud-provider-kind to v0.8.0 for Kubernetes image security fixes — still unused here.

Remaining 4.89.0 Resource Saver background container/image polling no longer wakes the engine. 4.88.0: HTTP 500 on startup/wake when the engine socket existed but was not yet listening; corrupted ~/.docker/daemon.json (null bytes after crash/power-loss) auto-recovers to defaults; docker ps port bindings include [::1]; Docker VMM inbound throughput regression (~0.3 GB/s) fixed.

Remaining 4.87.0 Windows: Store-installed WSL repeatedly prompted for wsl --update (also used by configure_docker_wsl_limits.ps1); misleading proxy errors named the destination instead of the unreachable upstream; Resource Saver / disk-limit UI fixes for Hyper-V and Docker VMM.

Pin 4.86.0 already includes unless-stopped / container-stop honoring on engine shutdown, VirtioFS AF_UNIX bidirectional sockets, OS-configured proxy Offload fix, and CVE-2026-17106 (docker container cp destination escape).
recommended_actions: Do not bump the Version default in scripts/update_docker_desktop.ps1 from this alert. Leave the pin at 4.86.0 until a human reviews 4.100.1 on this Windows host.
Do not change compose files, recovery scripts, or other stack config from this alert.

Treat 4.100.1 as the review target. 4.100.1 itself is additional rebranding only (no Security heading, no Known issues, no Updates, no Windows/WSL notes). Stack-relevant work is still remaining 4.100.0: Compose v5.7.1, WSL2 monodistro migration on next start (legacy dual-distro docker-desktop + docker-desktop-data), bind-mount file locks/ownership/notifications (desktop-feedback#765), and Hyper-V updates no longer enabling the WSL feature. Engine stays v29.9.3 from 4.99.0.

Before any 4.100.1 upgrade, snapshot or inspect the WSL/engine disk and note whether this host is still dual-distro (docker-desktop + docker-desktop-data). Remaining 4.100.0 migrates legacy dual-distro setups automatically on the next Desktop start. Do that in a planned window, not as an unattended winget. After the first start, confirm wsl -l -v, the data-disk path, .wslconfig limits, and that postgres/api/mcp plus *arr volumes are intact.

If taking 4.100.1, still plan a WSL 3.0.3 or later update in the same window for remaining 4.98.0 CVE-2026-112917. configure_docker_wsl_limits.ps1 already runs wsl --update; confirm the result is 3.0.3+ before treating the AF_VSOCK fix as done. Desktop alone is not the full official fix.

Still treat 4.98.0 CVE-2026-98432 kernel IPv4 TCP use-after-free and CVE-2026-112917 WSL 2 AF_VSOCK bypass as in-delta. 4.100.1, 4.100.0, and 4.99.0 do not re-list them — do not assume those fixes disappeared, and do not invent a new 4.100.1 CVE from the missing Security heading.

Still treat 4.97.0 CVE-2026-114409 leftover log/diagnostics cleanup and CVE-2026-99999 container TUN/AF_PACKET VM-network-stack corruption as in-delta. 4.100.1, 4.100.0, 4.99.0, and 4.98.0 do not re-list those two.

Still treat the 4.96.1–4.96.3 eMudhra intermediate-CA distrust (TLS intercept of Docker CLI/daemon; official notes assign no CVE id) as in-delta. 4.100.1, 4.100.0, and 4.99.0 are silent on eMudhra and remaining CA batches — do not assume that CA work is finished.

After any later 4.100.1 upgrade, confirm the WSL2 monodistro migration finished cleanly, WSL is 3.0.3+ (CVE-2026-112917), bind-mount create-then-lock/chown/notify works on media/*arr and ~/.garminconnect / ~/.endurance-coach (desktop-feedback#765), delete or sanitize diagnostics bundles and copies of Docker Desktop logs generated on 4.96.x or earlier (CVE-2026-114409 leftover cleartext API keys / OAuth tokens), and confirm Docker networking still works for ExpressVPN, media/*arr, and endurance-coach published ports after CVE-2026-98432 (kernel IPv4 TCP) and CVE-2026-99999 (VM network-stack corruption via TUN/AF_PACKET).

Ignore the 4.100.1 additional rebranding updates and the remaining 4.100.0 new look, Offload / dhictl / Agent bumps, ECI/kind, port-65535 hang, MCP Toolkit Profiles tab, docker build API hang, Docker VMM stopping-state / sparse-raw-disk / #820 VMM hang, WSL-not-installed Restart button, Mac privileged-port, and Linux AppArmor notes. Also ignore remaining 4.99.0 Offload / dhictl / Agent / Scout / Docker MCP CLI bumps, the Show-all-ports UI fix, Docker VMM published-port resets, Mac installer-killed-while-quitting, BuildKit-for-Windows-containers, and Windows-containers-at-login notes. Coach mcp is the endurance-coach container, not Docker's MCP toolkit. Do not switch this host to Docker VMM from the installer option.

Before any upgrade, confirm no media/*arr or other Compose network uses 192.168.65.0/24 (Docker Desktop's internal range). An overlap can leave the engine stuck on Starting until the network is removed (4.96.0 / desktop-feedback#659). 4.98.0 separately fixes the Starting page remaining after the engine is already up (#685).

Before any upgrade, confirm the Docker Desktop disk image / WSL data root is not under the installation directory (typically C:\Program Files\Docker). A 4.86.0-era path there can wipe engine disks (media volumes + postgres_data) on the way through 4.95.0. Also treat a busy/locked WSL data disk as a stop-ship until 4.96.0's mkfs-loop fix is understood. After 4.97.0, a Wsl/CallMsi/ installer error is not proof the disk was deleted.

Still treat 4.99.0 system-proxy socket leak on container HTTP via an upstream proxy, ungraceful shutdown skipping cleanup, Windows Update killing Desktop and corrupting engine databases, WSL 2 engine start racing a slow data disk, and WSL systemd-resolved flush every 30s (desktop-feedback#761) as in-delta.
Still treat 4.96.0 internal DHCP replies leaking onto the host LAN, engine-start hang on 192.168.65.0/24 overlap, and unusable WSL data disk triggering repeated mkfs attempts as in-delta.

Still treat 4.95.0 WSL data-disk deletion on update (desktop-feedback#667), Settings allowing that unsafe disk-image path, WinGet/update failure when app.asar is locked, and Hyper-V compact-after-restart as in-delta.

Still treat 4.94.0 WinGet/--always-run-service auto-start loss, the 4.92.0 WSL automount-timeout fix (desktop-feedback#695), Resource Saver pausing the VM before the Docker API is ready, and service-left-stopped-after-update as in-delta if upgrading from the 4.86.0 pin.

Before upgrading, check each WSL distro's /etc/wsl.conf for [automount] root=/ and avoid bind-mounting non-drive paths under /mnt (including /mnt/wslg). 4.94.0 explicitly fixes the 4.92.0 automount-timeout failure; 4.93.0 already had a related bind-mount proxy timeout fix.

If this host was installed with --always-run-service, plan to re-check the Docker Desktop service start mode after any WinGet upgrade (4.94.0 claims that auto-start is now preserved). Also confirm the engine is actually running after an update, not left stopped.

Still review remaining 4.93.0 items: unclean-shutdown start when engine recovery exceeds five minutes, WSL distro config.json crash that disabled integration, file-sharing list reset, Unix-socket port-forward host-path exposure, and UTF-8 BOM settings-store.json / daemon.json exit 151 (enable_docker_autostart.ps1 writes those files with Set-Content -Encoding UTF8).

Still review remaining 4.92.0 items if upgrading past the pin: published ports staying dead after a briefly busy host port, WSL2 bind-mount proxy serving stale/incomplete host dirs, WSL disk-image/kernel-module start hangs, containerd CVE-2026-53495.
Still review remaining 4.91.0 items: abrupt-shutdown network-DB recovery (was factory-reset-only), Compose rebuilds of endurance-coach on Resource Saver wake, idle-timeout 0 VM shutdown.

Before any upgrade, snapshot or inspect %APPDATA%\Docker\install-settings.json (and the all-users copy if present) so a WinGet hang on conflicting engine settings (still in 4.90.0) can be diagnosed. Do not save settings-store.json or daemon.json with a UTF-8 BOM (4.93.0 exit 151).

If upgrading later, run scripts/update_docker_desktop.ps1 only after a planned window; expect Docker restart plus heal_full_stack.ps1. Watch for the remaining 4.100.0 WSL2 monodistro migration on first start, bind-mount lock/ownership/notify regressions (#765), Windows Update / ungraceful shutdown corrupting engine DBs (4.99.0), proxy socket leaks until Desktop restart, WSL DNS cache flushes every 30s, WSL engine start racing a slow data disk, WSL below 3.0.3 leaving CVE-2026-112917 open, leftover Desktop log cleanup (CVE-2026-114409), VM network-stack failure from kernel TCP UAF (CVE-2026-98432) or a container TUN/AF_PACKET exploit (CVE-2026-99999), Starting page after the engine is already up, Request aborted on engine stop, desktop-linux context-file lock, file-share prefix matching, docker hang/Quit-dead after disk-full or console-host exit, a false WSL update prompt, a misleading disk-deleted dialog from Wsl/CallMsi/, TLS/registry failures from the eMudhra CA distrust landing in batches, LAN/VPN disruption from the pre-4.96.0 DHCP leak, engine-start hang on 192.168.65.0/24 overlap, WSL data-disk mkfs loops or deletion if the image path is under the install dir, app.asar lock during winget, the service not auto-starting after winget, Hyper-V compact/restart failure, 'Starting' hang, Resource Saver transient API errors on restart, engine recovery >5 min after unclean shutdown, published ports that never become reachable, stale media/*arr bind-mount listings, WSL integration dialogs during restarts, stuck-socket or corrupt-network-DB startup after power loss, and unexpected VM stop when idle timeout is 0.

After any upgrade, confirm WSL is 3.0.3 or later, the WSL2 layout is the expected monodistro (or a clean dual-distro leftover if migration did not apply), image pulls and registry TLS still work (CLI/daemon CA distrust), Compose v5.7.1 did not change media/*arr or endurance-coach behavior, Engine v29.9.3 is running, postgres/api/mcp (restart: unless-stopped) come back without a compose rebuild loop, published ports 5432/8000/8080 still bind, Docker/VM networking was not corrupted (CVE-2026-98432 / CVE-2026-99999), leftover 4.96.x-or-earlier Desktop logs/diagnostics were deleted or sanitized (CVE-2026-114409), the WSL/engine disk is intact (not reformatted; a 4.97.0 Wsl/CallMsi/ message is not proof it was deleted), file-sharing directories were not reset and still match whole directory names only (4.98.0 prefix-match fix), bind-mount create-then-lock/chown/notify works (#765), the Docker Desktop service is set to automatic start, host LAN/VPN still routes as expected, WSL DNS is stable (no 30s systemd-resolved flush), and host bind-mount contents/ownership on ~/.garminconnect and ~/.endurance-coach are complete and not 0:0.

If WSL fails to start, check the real wsl.exe error (not a 'bad magic string' or a 4.97.0 'disk file has been deleted' dialog from Wsl/CallMsi/; 4.98.0 should parse WSL 3.0.x codes more accurately), whether a remaining 4.100.0 monodistro migration is still in progress, whether the data disk was slow to appear (4.99.0), disk-image path access (and that it is not under the install directory), whether the data disk is already in use before any format, WSL kernel-module load, automount / bind-mount proxy timeouts, distro config.json, firmware/nested virtualization / hypervisor-at-startup, vfpext/VMP, and named third-party WSL plugins (Defender) rather than a missing Docker disk. Kind CVEs and 4.98.0 Kubernetes image tags can be ignored unless Kind/Offload Kubernetes is in use.
Use Automation Watchboard (yellow Update) as the cue to apply or skip 4.100.1 in Cursor.
